articles.body: A NestJS app upgrades from @nestjs/core 12.1 to 12.2 — npm i @nestjs/core@latest @nestjs/common@latest , nothing else touched. The test suite stays green. In production, an audit log that has recorded every failed signup for months — the field that failed, the message, and the full payload the user actually submitted — starts writing submittedPayload: undefined on every single entry. No exception, no crash, no warning in the logs. The validation itself still works exactly as before: bad input still gets rejected with a 400 . Only the forensic trail disappeared. This is written against @nestjs/core 12.2.0 (verified 2026-10-20 via npm view @nestjs/core dist-tags and the official v12.2.0 release notes ; 12.0.0 shipped 2026-08-27, and the 11.x line remains on the legacy npm tag at 11.2.7 ).

articles.title: HTML Semantic Tags Explained: header, nav, main, article, section and footer
articles.excerpt: Originally published on CodingCush. HTML semantic tags are elements that clearly describe their meaning and the type of content inside them, for both browsers and people reading the code. Tags such as…
articles.body: Originally published on CodingCush . HTML semantic tags are elements that clearly describe their meaning and the type of content inside them, for both browsers and people reading the code. Tags such as header, nav, main, article, section and footer tell everyone what each part of a page is for, without guessing from class names. A header is for introductory content, nav is for main links, main holds the primary content, article holds a self contained piece, section groups related content, and footer holds closing information. Using them makes your pages easier to read, more accessible for screen readers, and clearer for search engines. What Are Semantic Tags, in Simple Words? The word semantic simply means related to meaning. A semantic tag carries meaning in its name.

articles.title: Python Function Arguments Explained: Positional, Keyword, Default, *args and **kwargs
articles.excerpt: Originally published on CodingCush. Python function arguments are the values you pass into a function when you call it, so the function can work with real data instead of fixed values. You can pass th…
articles.body: Originally published on CodingCush . Python function arguments are the values you pass into a function when you call it, so the function can work with real data instead of fixed values. You can pass them by position, by name, or not at all if the function has a default value. Python also lets a function accept any number of extra values, using *args for positional values and **kwargs for named values. Learn these five styles and you can read most function definitions calmly and write flexible functions of your own. Parameters and Arguments: What Is the Difference? A parameter is the variable name inside the brackets when you define a function. An argument is the actual value you send when you call it.

articles.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
articles.excerpt: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
articles.body: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

articles.excerpt: "Earlier on in my life, even before 'The Martian,' I wanted to bring back audio-only entertainment."
articles.body: Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled " Exoplanet ." Weir (" The Martian ") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible. The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements.

articles.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
articles.excerpt: Blue Origin has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the launcher even more flexible and capable. The company has also built a new engine, called Northstar.
articles.body: Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment.
